captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a two-part sliding clamp assembly designed for 3D printing. It consists of a long, flat rectangular guide rod with an integrated fixed jaw at one end, and a separate sliding jaw designed to mount onto the rod. Both jaws feature a tapered profile, a small hook at their outer tips, and a triangular V-shaped cutout on their inner clamping faces to securely grip round or angled objects.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric sliding clamp in OpenSCAD with a main rectangular guide rod, a fixed jaw at one end, and a separate sliding jaw. Ensure the design is highly adjustable by defining parameters for the rod length, rod width, rod thickness, jaw length, jaw width, V-notch depth, and clearance for the slider opening.
captions.factory: The code defines the assembly using modular parts: 'hook' (using a cube primitive), 'vee' (using a rotated cube for the V-notch), and 'Jaw' (using a difference of cubes, rotated cubes, hooks, and vees to form the tapered clamping arm). The 'rod' module combines a long cube with one integrated jaw. The 'slider' module creates a hollow sleeve using a difference of cubes (incorporating clearance parameters) and attaches a slightly shorter jaw to it. Finally, 'print_part' arranges the main rod and the rotated sliding jaw side-by-side for flat 3D printing.
